text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, even for someone who did not write it. One key habit is following naming conventions: use clear, meaningful names for variables and functions so their purpose is obvious. Another important idea is to keep functions small and focused on one task. This makes the code simpler to test and reuse. Clean code is also easier to maintain, because fixing bugs or adding new features takes less time when the structure is clear. In short, writing clean code saves effort for the whole team.
